extracted.intended_audience: regulated industry (food/additive/drug manufacturers), federal contractors, procurement officials, and members of the public who submit objections/comments
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive regulatory requirements and standards excerpted from Federal Register rulemaking and regulatory orders covering pesticide tolerances, food additives, drug certification, flood-control operations, and defense procurement policies. Useful for parties preparing objections/comments, certification submissions, contract clauses, or compliance actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing objections to an order (general procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person adversely affected may within 30 days from date of publication file with the Hearing Clerk, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, Room 5440, 330 Independence Avenue SW., Washington, D.C. 20201, written objections, preferably in quintuplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections shall show wherein the person filing will be adversely affected, and specify with particularity the provisions of the order deemed objectionable and the grounds for the objections. If a hearing is requested, objections must state the issues for the hearing. A hearing will be granted if the objections are supported by grounds legally sufficient to justify the relief sought. Objections may be accompanied by a memorandum or brief in support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of order
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall become effective on the date of its publication in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraquat tolerances (residue limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerances established for residues of paraquat (l,l'-dimethyl-4,4'-bipyridinium) calculated as the cation in or on raw agricultural commodities: 0.5 part per million (negligible residue) in or on almond hulls, cottonseed, potatoes, sugar beets, sugar beet tops; 0.05 part per million in or on almonds, apples, apricots, avocados, bananas, cherries, citrus, coffee beans, corn (fresh vegetable), corn fodder and forage, corn grain, figs, filberts, grapes, lettuce, macadamia nuts, melons, nectarines, olives, papaya, peaches, pears, peppers, plums (fresh prunes), sorghum forage, sorghum grain, soybeans, soybean forage, tomatoes, walnuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tolerances set forth are established by the order except for cottonseed and potatoes which were established by prior orders. Secretary of Agriculture certified pesticide chemical is useful for purposes for which tolerances are being established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to food-additive use limitations (vinylidene chloride copolymer coatings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deletion of prior sentence limiting finished vinylidene chloride copolymer coatings containing units derived from methyl acrylate and/or methacrylic acid to use in contact with nonalcoholic foods having a pH above 5.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After amendment, additional uses of such copolymers as food-contact coatings on nylon film are permitted as described in the regulation change; parties affected may file objections as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubber articles intended for repeated use — permitted elastomers and specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific polymers and compositional limits are authorized for rubber articles intended for repeated food contact use, e.g., ethylene-propylene-1,4-hexadiene copolymers containing no more than 6 weight percent of total polymer units derived from 1,4-hexadiene; vinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene copolymers (minimum number average molecular weight 70,000 as determined by osmotic pressure in methyl ethyl ketone); vinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene-tetrafluoroethylene copolymers (minimum number average molecular weight 100,000 as determined likewise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized materials are alphabetically inserted/modified in the regulation text; specific numeric limits and MW determination method (osmotic pressure in methyl ethyl ketone) are part of the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubber vulcanization materials — cross-linking agent use limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain vulcanizing/cross-linking agents are permitted only for specified elastomers and limited to defined use levels, e.g., 4,4'-Bis(aminocyclohexyl)methane carbamate only as cross-linking agent in vulcanization of specified copolymers and limited to use at levels not to exceed 2.4 percent by weight of such copolymers; hexamethylenediamine carbamate similarly limited to not to exceed 1.5 percent by weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use is restricted to the named elastomers identified in the regulation; limits are weight-percent of the copolymer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additives and residual emulsifier limits in rubber formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Activators (total not to exceed 5 percent by weight of rubber product except magnesium oxide may be used at higher levels). Miscellaneous substances total not to exceed 5 percent by weight. A specified omega-hydroxypoly(oxyethylene) phosphate barium salt emulsifier for residual polymerization is permitted only as residual polymerization emulsifier at levels not to exceed 0.7 percent by weight of specified copolymers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent limits refer to weight of the rubber product or copolymer as specified; permissible uses are constrained by the regulation's subdivision headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification standards for triacetyloleandomycin chewable tablets — identity/strength/quality/purity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each triacetyloleandomycin chewable tablet shall contain an amount of triacetyloleandomycin equivalent to 125 milligrams of oleandomycin with suitable diluents, binders, buffers, colorings, and flavorings. The moisture content is not more than 5 percent. The triacetyloleandomycin used conforms to standards prescribed by § 148m.2(a) or is recognized in the U.S.P. or N.F. and conforms to standards prescribed by such official compendium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the 'standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity' required for certification; any other substance used must conform to its recognized standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirement for certified drug
rubrics_metrics.description: Triacetyloleandomycin chewable tablets shall be labeled in accordance with the requirements of § 148.3 of this chapter. Its expiration date is 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for certification — required test results
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification requests must include results of tests and assays on the triacetyloleandomycin used in making the batch for potency, toxicity, moisture, pH, residue on ignition, identity, Rf value, acetyl value (only if more than one spot is present in the determination of Rf value), and crystallinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data supplement the general requirements of § 146.2 of this chapter and are required to support certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples required for certification submissions (drug)
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples required: triacetyloleandomycin used in making the batch — 10 packages (nine ~500 mg each and one ~2 g); the batch — a minimum of 30 tablets; in an initial request, each other ingredient used in making the batch — one package of each containing approximately 5 grams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified package sizes and counts when submitting samples for certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification fees (drug)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees: $0.75 for each tablet in the sample submitted in accordance with subparagraph (3)(ii)(b); $4 for each container submitted in accordance with subparagraph (3)(ii)(c); $5 for each container submitted in accordance with subparagraph (3)(ii)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are assessed based on the type and container of samples submitted for certification testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests and methods of assay — potency procedure and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Potency: prepare sample stock by placing representative number of tablets in glass blending jar with sufficient 80 percent isopropanol to give 1,000 micrograms per milliliter. Use plate assay with dilutions in 0.2M potassium phosphate buffer pH 10.5 or turbidimetric assay in 1 percent potassium phosphate buffer pH 6.0. Potency is satisfactory if it contains not less than 90 percent nor more than 125 percent of the amount represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified solvents, stock concentration, buffer pH depending on assay method; acceptance criterion is 90–125% of labeled amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moisture testing (drug)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moisture test: Proceed as directed in § 141a.5(a) of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moisture content must not exceed 5 percent for certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice/public-procedure exception for drug certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the conditions prerequisite to providing for certification of the subject drug have been complied with and it is in the public interest not to delay, notice and public procedure and delayed effective date are not prerequisites to this promulgation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order is effective upon publication in the Federal Register in such cases where statutory and data prerequisites are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood control operation objective (Arbuckle Dam)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate Arbuckle Dam and Lake in the interest of flood control to reduce as much as practicable the flood damage below the lake. Flood control discharges shall be limited to amounts which, when combined with local inflows below the dam, will not produce flows in excess of bank-full on Rock Creek downstream of the lake and on the Washita River from confluence of Rock Creek to Durwood, Okla.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating stages and corresponding flows are specified: an 11-foot stage (15,000 c.f.s.) on the USGS gage on Rock Creek near Dougherty, Okla., river mile 1; and a 20-foot stage (15,000 c.f.s.) on the USGS gage on the Washita River near Durwood, Okla., river mile 63.4. Use these metrics to limit releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood release rule when lake exceeds top of flood control pool
rubrics_metrics.description: When the level in Lake of the Arbuckles exceeds elevation 885.3 (top of flood control pool), releases shall be made at the maximum rate possible through the river outlet works and the uncontrolled spillway and continued until the lake level recedes to elevation 885.3, when releases shall be made to equal inflow or the maximum release permissible under paragraph (a), whichever is greater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood control reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative in immediate charge shall furnish daily to the District Engineer a report showing lake elevation; number of river outlet works gates in operation with respective openings and releases; uncontrolled spillway release; municipal pumping rate; tail water elevation; available evaporation data; and precipitation in inches. Normally readings at 8 a.m., noon, 4 p.m., and midnight shall be shown each day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever lake level rises to elevation 872 and releases for flood regulation are necessary or appear imminent, report at once by telephone or telegraph and then report once daily in that manner until the lake level recedes to elevation 872. These latter reports shall reach the District Engineer by 9 a.m. each day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary modification of flood regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations governing use of flood control storage above elevation 872 are subject to temporary modification in time of flood by the District Engineer if found desirable on the basis of conditions at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such desired modifications shall be communicated to the representative of the Bureau of Reclamation by any available means and confirmed in writing under date of the same day to the Regional Director in charge of the locality and his designated agent, with a copy to the representative in charge of the Arbuckle Dam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood operations must not restrict municipal/industrial pumping or downstream releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Flood control operation shall not restrict pumping necessary for municipal and industrial uses and releases necessary for downstream users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood releases subject to dam protection and safe-routing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases made in accordance with the regulations are subject to the condition that releases shall not be made at rates or in a manner that would be inconsistent with emergency requirements for protecting the dam and lake from major damage or inconsistent with the safe routing of the inflow design flood (spillway design flood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain outlet works discharge characteristics per construction plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The discharge characteristics of the river outlet works (capable of discharging approximately 1,880 c.f.s. when lake level is at 872) shall be maintained in accordance with the construction plans (Bureau of Reclamation Specifications No. 6099 as modified by 'as built' drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All elevations stated are at Arbuckle Dam and referred to the datum in use at that location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government personnel conduct in procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: All governmental personnel engaged in procurement and related activities shall conduct business dealing with industry in a manner above reproach in every respect; transactions relating to expenditure of public funds require the highest degree of public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official conduct must be such that the individual would have no reticence about making a full public disclosure thereof; see cited service regulations for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational conflicts of interest — contracting officer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officer is responsible for applying DoD Directive 5500.10 rules to contracts under his cognizance and shall determine whether each proposed procurement is subject to the Directive. If a potential conflict exists, before issuing solicitation he must prepare a written analysis identifying which of the four rules (or other conflict) is applicable and recommend a solicitation notice and clause to avoid the conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clause shall spell out specific future restrictions on the contractor and have a specific time period of effectiveness. Time effectiveness should be a fixed term of reasonable duration measured to avoid unfair competitive advantage, except where Rule 1 is involved (permanent). After approval, include determination and analysis in negotiation file and incorporate the approved notice/clause in solicitation subject to negotiation. Clause must not defer determination of applicability until after award. For Rule 4 situations, ensure agreement is executed and copies made available to Government. Do not impose restrictions in follow-on procurements absent a specific contractual agreement. Departments must maintain records of solicitation notices and clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncollusive bids and proposals certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote full and free competition, a certification against collusion shall be included in all (1) invitations for bids and (2) requests for proposals or quotations (with specified exceptions), involving firm fixed-price contracts and fixed-price contracts with escalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When solicitation authorizes submission of oral offers and requires confirmation in writing, the solicitation shall require that the certification be included with or be expressly incorporated by reference in and thereby made part of the confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement of natural rubber — required purchases from National Stockpile (GSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is national policy to require contractors to purchase natural rubber from the National Stockpile (General Services Administration) in connection with specified defense contracts for tires, tubes, recapping materials and related contracts, except where subcontracting provisions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clause 'Purchase of Natural Rubber' prescribes ordering procedures (Manager, Rubber Project, GSA address), states that rubber purchased may be used in any manner the Contractor desires, except subcontract rules: when subcontracting, contractor not required to purchase but must incorporate same terms into subcontracts and forward one copy of each such subcontract to GSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warranty clause policy and factors for use in Government contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A warranty clause gives the Government contractual rights to assert claims regarding deficiencies of supplies or services after acceptance and may allow additional time to assert rights. A warranty clause shall be used when found to be in the Government's best interest after analysis of certain factors and shall not be included in cost-reimbursement type contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any warranty clause shall not limit rights afforded by the Inspection clause relating to latent defects, fraud, and gross mistakes amounting to fraud. Care should be taken to ensure consistency between the warranty clause and other warranty provisions. The decision to use a warranty clause is made by the Head of a Procuring Activity or designee. Factors to consider include: (1) nature of the item and its end use; (2) cost of the warranty and degree of price competition; (3) criticalness of achieving specified performance capabilities and design specifications; (4) cost of correction or replacement in the absence of a warranty; (5) administrative cost and difficulty.
